final_candidates.decision_summary: Disrupts the N157-X-T156 glycosylation sequon, a well-established antibody escape mechanism in arenavirus GPC. Highest MSA frequency (0.308) and perfect PLM score (1.0) among all candidates support viability and cell entry preservation.

Conservative aromatic-to-aromatic substitution at an epitope-proximal position likely involved in antibody contact. Perfect PLM score (1.0) supports structural viability despite low MSA frequency (0.038), mitigated by the conservative nature of the change.

Removal of a positively charged side chain likely involved in antibody paratope interaction, providing a plausible escape mechanism. Perfect PLM score (1.0) supports viability, though low MSA frequency (0.045) introduces some uncertainty about evolutionary tolerance.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool has converged after three rounds of evidence integration; the phenotype tool provided no applicable scores and all other tools have been exhausted on the final candidates, making further rounds uninformative.

history.rationale: Position N157 lies in the GP1 receptor-binding region and is a known antibody contact site for neutralizing antibodies targeting the GPC trimer interface; charge reversal may disrupt antibody binding while preserving receptor interaction.
Phenotype and toxin tools returned not_applicable; no evidence to change confidence. Retaining based on structural knowledge of GP1 epitope region near antibody contact sites.

Highest MSA frequency (0.308) and perfect PLM score (1.0) strongly support viability. Position 157 is in the known Arevirumab-3 epitope, and N→K introduces a charge change likely to disrupt antibody contacts.

Highest MSA z-score (0.308) and perfect PLM (1.000) indicate strong viability. N157 is part of an N-linked glycosylation motif; disrupting this glycan site is a well-known immune escape mechanism in arenavirus glycoproteins.
N157K disrupts the N-X-T glycosylation sequon (N157-T156), a well-established antibody escape mechanism. Highest MSA frequency (0.308) and perfect PLM (1.0) among candidates support viability.
Adjacent to known epitope residues in the GP1 subunit; removal of a hydroxyl group may alter local hydrogen bonding with antibody CDRs without disrupting the overall fold.
No applicable evidence returned. Retaining based on proximity to known neutralizing antibody epitope cluster.
Zero MSA frequency and only moderate PLM (0.545) weaken this candidate significantly. T→A is a subtle change unlikely to dramatically disrupt antibody binding.

Zero MSA frequency and low PLM (0.545) indicate poor evolutionary and computational tolerance. T156 may be part of the N157 glycosylation sequon (N-X-T), and its mutation could destabilize the glycan attachment context.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA frequency and low PLM (0.545) indicate poor evolutionary and computational tolerance. T156 may be part of the N157 glycosylation sequon (N-X-T), and its mutation could destabilize the glycan attachment context.

history.rationale: Position K163 is in the GP1 globular head near the antibody epitope cluster for Arevirumab-3 components; charge reversal could disrupt electrostatic contacts with CDR loops.
No applicable evidence returned. Charge reversal at a surface-exposed position in the epitope region is a plausible escape strategy.
High PLM (0.958) supports viability but zero MSA frequency is concerning. Charge reversal K→E is excellent for disrupting antibody contacts but evolutionary novelty raises some viability risk.
High PLM (0.958) but zero MSA frequency and charge reversal raise concerns about functional impact on receptor binding or GP1-GP2 interface stability.

Zero MSA frequency indicates no natural homolog carries this substitution, suggesting poor evolutionary tolerance despite high PLM. Charge reversal (K→E) may disrupt local electrostatics needed for GP1-GP2 interaction.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA frequency indicates no natural homolog carries this substitution, suggesting poor evolutionary tolerance despite high PLM. Charge reversal (K→E) may disrupt local electrostatics needed for GP1-GP2 interaction.

history.rationale: D160 is in the GP1 head domain near known neutralizing antibody contact residues; alanine substitution removes a charged side chain potentially involved in antibody paratope interactions.
No applicable evidence returned. Retaining as a surface-exposed charged residue in the epitope region.
Moderate MSA frequency (0.192) and good PLM (0.850) support viability. D→A removes a negative charge that may contact antibodies, but the effect may be less dramatic than charge reversals.
Moderate MSA (0.192) and good PLM (0.850) support viability. Removing a negative charge at an epitope position may reduce antibody affinity.
Moderate MSA (0.192) but only moderate PLM (0.850). D160 may participate in salt bridges stabilizing the GP1 fold; removing the carboxylate risks local destabilization affecting entry.

rejection.reason: Moderate MSA (0.192) but only moderate PLM (0.850). D160 may participate in salt bridges stabilizing the GP1 fold; removing the carboxylate risks local destabilization affecting entry.

history.rationale: Y155 is in the GP1 receptor-binding domain; conservative aromatic substitution may subtly alter antibody contact surface while preserving hydrophobic packing and receptor binding.
No applicable evidence returned. Conservative substitution removing a hydroxyl group that may participate in antibody H-bonding.

Perfect PLM score (1.0) indicates high viability despite low MSA frequency. Y→F removes the hydroxyl H-bond donor critical for antibody recognition while preserving the aromatic ring, making it an excellent escape mutation.

Perfect PLM score (1.000) supports viability despite low MSA frequency. Conservative aromatic-to-aromatic change at a surface-exposed epitope position likely alters antibody contacts while preserving local structure.
Conservative aromatic substitution with perfect PLM (1.0) supports structural viability. Low MSA (0.038) is a minor concern but the conservative nature mitigates risk to folding.
N119 is in the GP1 subunit near the base of the receptor-binding platform; mutation to lysine introduces a charge change that may disrupt antibody contacts in the Arevirumab epitope region.
Position 119 is in the GP1 core region more likely involved in structural integrity than antibody contact. Prioritizing epitope-proximal positions instead.

rejection.reason: Position 119 is in the GP1 core region more likely involved in structural integrity than antibody contact. Prioritizing epitope-proximal positions instead.

history.rationale: S153 is in the GP1 head domain; proline introduction may alter local backbone conformation and disrupt antibody epitope geometry while potentially being tolerated in a loop region.
No applicable evidence returned. Proline introduction may disrupt local backbone conformation relevant to antibody recognition.
Low MSA frequency (0.038) and low PLM (0.540) indicate poor viability. Proline introduction may disrupt local backbone conformation needed for proper folding.

rejection.reason: Low MSA frequency (0.038) and low PLM (0.540) indicate poor viability. Proline introduction may disrupt local backbone conformation needed for proper folding.

history.rationale: R161 is a charged residue in the GP1 globular head near known neutralizing antibody contact sites; alanine substitution removes a key electrostatic interaction point.
No applicable evidence returned. Removing a large charged side chain from a surface-exposed epitope position.
Perfect PLM score (1.0) supports viability. R→A removes a positively charged side chain that likely forms salt bridges or H-bonds with antibody CDRs, providing strong escape potential.
Perfect PLM (1.000) indicates high plausibility. Removing a charged arginine side chain at an epitope-proximal position likely disrupts electrostatic contacts with neutralizing antibodies.
Perfect PLM (1.0) and removal of a charged side chain likely involved in antibody paratope contact make this a strong escape candidate. Low MSA (0.045) is offset by high computational plausibility.
G159 is in the GP1 head domain; introduction of a charged aspartate may create steric/electrostatic clash with antibody CDRs while the position may tolerate substitution due to surface exposure.
Glycine at 159 may be structurally important for backbone flexibility; introducing a charged residue here risks destabilizing the local fold needed for receptor binding.

rejection.reason: Glycine at 159 may be structurally important for backbone flexibility; introducing a charged residue here risks destabilizing the local fold needed for receptor binding.

history.rationale: L164 is in the GP1 head domain near the antibody epitope cluster; alanine substitution reduces hydrophobic contact surface potentially used by antibody paratopes.
No applicable evidence returned. Retaining at lower confidence as a hydrophobic-to-small substitution in the epitope region.
Very low PLM score (0.356) indicates this mutation is poorly tolerated. L164 likely plays a structural role, and its mutation may compromise protein stability and cell entry.

rejection.reason: Very low PLM score (0.356) indicates this mutation is poorly tolerated. L164 likely plays a structural role, and its mutation may compromise protein stability and cell entry.
